name: accordion
pattern: An open-and-close component for headings, buttons, and panels following the APG Accordion Pattern
responsibility: Opens and closes panels with buttons inside user-authored headings and provides aria-expanded, aria-controls, data-state, and cancelable toggle events. It does not generate appearance or content

authorMarkup.trigger: A native <button type="button"> with data-accordion-target="trigger". The APG Accordion Pattern requires the button to be inside a heading element, but heading levels are determined by the page's document structure and cannot be decided by the library, so this contract neither requires nor validates a heading. The user writes the heading
authorMarkup.panel: An element with data-accordion-target="panel". Place them in the same order as the triggers
authorMarkup.label: The user writes the trigger label
authorMarkup.content: The controller does not generate elements or content
authorMarkup.nativeAlternative: Use the disclosure controller when a single <details> is sufficient or when multiple <details> elements with the same name provide the required exclusive control. Use this component for DOM structures where a panel cannot be a sibling of its trigger

semanticElements: There must be at least one trigger target
Each trigger must be an HTMLButtonElement with type="button"
The number of panel targets must equal the number of trigger targets
Triggers and panels must be descendants of the root
contractValidation.invalidMarkup: Validate the markup on connection. If it violates the contract, the controller does not apply ARIA, listeners, state output, or open-and-close behavior, and calls console.warn once while connected. It does not throw
contractValidation.warning: The warning includes the accordion controller, the expected native <button type="button"> triggers, and the same number of panels. Enhancement has been disabled.
contractValidation.notGuaranteed: The APG Accordion Pattern requirements that a trigger be inside a heading element and that the heading level be valid are not validated. These are document-structure concerns for the page and cannot be determined by the controller

completion.warning: The completion warning lists the added attributes: "Added <attributes>. Include them in your markup." It is emitted once while connected, using a separate flag from the enhancement-disabled warning

multiple.description: Whether multiple panels can be open at the same time. When false, opening one panel closes the others

open.description: Indexes of panels open initially. Used only when the markup has no open-and-close state
An array of indexes for open panels. The setter changes open-and-close state and state output without dispatching a custom event

show(index).description: Opens the panel at the specified index. Does not dispatch a custom event

hide(index).description: Closes the panel at the specified index. Does not dispatch a custom event

toggle(index).description: Toggles the panel at the specified index. Does not dispatch a custom event

accordion:beforetoggle.when: Immediately before opening or closing from a trusted trigger activation

detail.open: The open-and-close state about to be committed
detail.previousOpen: The open-and-close state before the change

accordion:beforetoggle.effect: When preventDefault() is called, do not change open-and-close state, ARIA, state output, or accordion:toggle

accordion:toggle.when: After opening or closing from a trusted trigger activation is committed

detail.previousOpen: The open-and-close state before the change

events.exclusive: When multiple is false, closing other panels for exclusivity does not dispatch an event. Events are dispatched only for the panel targeted by the user's operation
events.programmatic: The open setter, show(), hide(), toggle(), initialization, and reconnection do not dispatch custom events
events.synthetic: A click with isTrusted=false does not dispatch a custom event and only synchronizes open-and-close state and state output

consumerIntegration.stimulusActions: accordion:toggle and accordion:beforetoggle can be received on the root or an ancestor. The controller does not stop event propagation
consumerIntegration.cancelableHook: To stop opening or closing, call event.preventDefault() in an accordion:beforetoggle listener
consumerIntegration.programmatic: Another controller can read and write open through a Stimulus controller reference or outlets. The programmatic API does not dispatch events
consumerIntegration.nested: When receiving events from a nested accordion on the outside, limit the target to the root with :self or event.target === event.currentTarget

behavior.initial: Prioritize the panel's hidden attribute and apply the open value only when the markup has no open-and-close state
behavior.pointer: A trusted click on a valid trigger commits opening or closing through beforetoggle with reason="pointer"
behavior.keyboard: Use activation by Enter and Space on the native button. The APG Accordion Pattern does not require arrow keys between headings, so the controller does not implement arrow keys, Home, End, or Ctrl+Page Up/Down
behavior.exclusive: When multiple is false, opening one panel closes the other panels. All panels may be closed; there is no requirement that one always remain open
behavior.disabled: A trigger with native button.disabled true or aria-disabled="true" does not activate. The APG Accordion Pattern recommends aria-disabled for a header that cannot be collapsed. Native disabled also prevents focus, which would make the existence of an unopenable panel unreachable to keyboard users, so both are checked. Do not add data-* for disabled. The public API can change state regardless of disabled status

managedMarkup.trigger: Synchronize aria-expanded with open-and-close state. Point to the corresponding panel ID only when aria-controls is not specified
managedMarkup.panel: Generate an ID only when one is not specified. Synchronize hidden with open-and-close state
managedMarkup.role: Do not add role="region" to panels. It can create too many landmarks in an accordion with many simultaneously open panels, so the user may write it when needed
managedMarkup.stateOnly: The controller-managed state output consists only of root, trigger, and panel data-state
managedMarkup.preservation: Do not overwrite id, role, aria-controls, or other attributes authored earlier by the user. The controller synchronizes aria-expanded and hidden

stateOutputs.ownership: Only trigger and panel data-state are controller-owned; do not express state with ARIA attributes
stateOutputs.root: Do not emit data-state. Opening and closing are per-item states and are not aggregated on the root. The user derives "whether one or more are open" with CSS :has([data-state="open"])

lifecycle: Register click and keydown listeners on triggers only while the markup is valid, and remove them when the markup becomes invalid and in disconnect(). Because listeners are not registered for invalid markup, register them in reconcile() rather than connect()
Track added and removed trigger and panel targets with Stimulus TargetConnected/TargetDisconnected
Leave generated ARIA, IDs, data-state, and hidden in place in disconnect()
On reconnection, synchronize ARIA and state output with the current markup without reapplying the initial open value
Do not duplicate listeners or custom events when reconnecting the same instance

observations.impact: The contract fixes native trigger activation, aria-expanded, and panel visibility; compatibility wording does not choose these semantics.

acceptanceCriteria: The behavior and accessibility implemented by this component must meet WCAG 2.2 Level AA.

The AAA to achieve is 2.1.3 Keyboard (No Exception) (no feature is reachable only by pointer) and 3.2.5 Change on Request (the controller moves focus only through user operation or a call from the user's JS, and never through a timer)
Only trusted trigger activation dispatches one cancelable beforetoggle and one toggle after commitment, in that order
Canceling beforetoggle does not change open-and-close state, ARIA, state output, or the toggle event
aria-expanded and aria-controls express the trigger-to-panel relationship, and IDs do not collide within the page
The controller does not implement arrow keys, and Tab order remains native
The public API, initialization, and reconnection synchronize open-and-close state and state output without dispatching custom events
Invalid markup disables enhancement with one warning
Automated tests pass in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit
Report the open-and-close state announcements from a screen reader on a real device as unverified
